intent: Commit hook keeps its own files out of the commit
notes: The pre-commit hook no longer stages its status and whiteboard files. A blocked commit's retry therefore sees exactly the change the Architect approved (#102).

When generated hook files are staged by accident (for example by `git add -A` in a repository that still tracks old copies), the hook removes them from that commit attempt and says so. A staged deletion of those files, which is what `gator update` produces, is kept so the migration can be committed.
The Enterprise hook is unchanged: the Enterprise server still reads a committed status file.

`gator update` now removes old tracked copies of all four hook files from the Git index (#78). The files stay on disk. A dry run and the JSON plan predict this, and the update untracks exactly what it predicted. The terminal and the Dashboard both show "Gator removed N hook-ephemera paths from the Git index…" with the exact paths and an explanation. The one-time staged deletion is meant to be committed with the update. Enterprise-managed repositories keep their status and whiteboard files tracked.
The governance guidance no longer says hook files "may appear modified" as normal; it explains the migration instead.

Coding loops no longer mark an approved change as stale, or a landed commit as different, just because a hook-owned file was staged or left out. They compare a named "governed" fingerprint that excludes only those hook files; raw Git trees stay recorded and remain what reviewers diff. Older loop sessions keep comparing raw trees.

A new `gator hook override acknowledge` command records the Architect's decision to keep every current dangerous-pattern finding in one step. It writes the keys, the Architect's name and one acknowledgement line per finding into the commit draft, checks the result with the same validator the hook uses, and writes nothing if the findings moved, the set is incomplete, or the Architect name conflicts. Agents use it only after the Architect replies "Acknowledged" to an enumerated prompt.

The Dashboard's blocked-commit dialog can now record a pause decision: it lists every current paused finding and records them all with one **Acknowledged** confirmation, asking for a name only when none is known. Closing the dialog is labelled "Close without resolving" and says the commit still pauses; nothing in the Dashboard claims a pause is resolved unless the decision was written.
